subject: Boston Avenue Zoning Veto Override
overview: The Council overrode the Mayor's veto of the Boston Avenue Neighborhood Corridor District zoning, maintaining 'by right' status for purpose-built student housing. The meeting also featured testimony regarding firefighter contract disputes and allegations of political targeting using the police department.

items.title: Ceremonial Items and Announcements
items.summary: Approved several local event announcements and recognized Councilor Leming for his return from military service.

items.title: Minutes and Committee Reports
items.summary: Approved the records of the September 29th meeting and a committee report regarding the next phase of the city's zoning project.

items.title: Fire Department Labor Disputes and Legal Audit
items.summary: Referred questions to the administration regarding firefighter contract stipends and requested an outside audit of city legal practices after the union reported losing 20 out of 21 recent legal challenges.

items.title: School Reappropriations
items.summary: Approved the reallocation of capital funds to address intercom system replacements and chiller repairs at multiple schools.

items.title: PILOT and Community Benefits Framework
items.summary: Referred a resolution to the Committee of the Whole to establish a new framework for negotiating payments in lieu of taxes (PILOT) and community benefits with Tufts University.

items.title: Boston Avenue Zoning Veto Override
items.summary: Overrode the Mayor's veto of the Boston Avenue Neighborhood Corridor District zoning amendments to maintain 'by right' status for student housing in the BA3 subdistrict.

items.title: Administrative and Budgetary Tabling
items.summary: Tabled various items including city charter implementations, police chief search funding, and supplemental legal appropriations to future meetings.

items.title: Allegations of Political Intimidation
items.summary: Heard a public petition regarding an alleged politically motivated police investigation initiated by the Mayor into local organizers, which councilors characterized as an abuse of power.
